name: Gold
occurrence: Found natively as nuggets and veins in quartz rock, and dispersed in seawater at extremely low concentration.
notableCharacteristics: One of only two metallic elements with a natural colour other than silvery-grey (the other being copper), a striking effect caused by relativistic quantum effects on its electrons that no simpler theory predicts.
whyHere: Gold's electrons move fast enough that relativistic effects noticeably shrink and reshape its outer orbitals, shifting which wavelengths of light it absorbs — a genuinely unusual quantum-relativistic explanation for why gold looks golden rather than silvery like nearly every other metal.
didYouKnow: Explaining gold's colour actually requires Einstein's special relativity — its innermost electrons move fast enough that relativistic effects shift its light absorption into the blue range, making the reflected light look yellow-gold.
genZNote: Doesn't oxidize easily, conducts well, and refuses to lose its shine. Also its whole colour needs actual relativity to explain. Icon behavior.
